cases.reason: The goal specifies adding an Export CSV button on the Thimblevane shop admin Orders page, the details state who it is for along with the required columns and date-filter behavior, and the acceptance criteria describe concrete, checkable outcomes.

The task clearly specifies making password reset links on the Quillmoor members site expire after 30 minutes, details the expired-link page text, resend button, and reused-link behavior, and includes checkable acceptance criteria for links opened before and after 30 minutes.

The goal specifies adding a print stylesheet to the Larkspur Kitchen blog's recipe pages, the details state who it is for and what to include or hide, and the first acceptance criterion can be directly checked by printing the Barley Soup recipe to PDF.

The goal specifies changing scripts/backup.sh to append one line per run to /var/log/tallowmere-backup.log, the details state who it is for and what each line must include, and the build criteria define concrete, checkable outcomes for successful and failed runs.

The goal specifies what to change and where (showing the event's time zone after the start time in Hollowbrook events app invitation messages), the details specify who it is for and what to include (the short zone name for guests in other countries), and two acceptance criteria define concrete, checkable outputs for Europe/Berlin and America/New_York events.

The goal specifies what to show and where on the Driftwood help centre search results page, the goal and details state who it is for and what must be included, and the build criterion names a concrete result that can be checked.

The goal specifies the exact rate-limit headers to add and where, the details explain who they serve and that the 600-calls-per-hour limit must stay unchanged, and the acceptance criteria define observable header values and decrement behavior that a reviewer can check.

The goal specifies creating docs/onboarding/first-day.md in the Tallowmere repository, the details define the audience, required content, and constraints, and the acceptance criteria provide concrete, checkable conditions.
The goal specifies the exact heading change and location on the Thimblevane shop's About page, and the build criterion provides a concrete, verifiable check that the heading reads Our story.

The goal clearly specifies what to change and where (raising the idle sign-out time from 15 to 60 minutes on the Quillmoor members site), states who it is for (members reading long articles), and includes a checkable acceptance criterion.

The goal clearly states what to change and where (adding exact alt text to the map image on the Contact page of the Larkspur Kitchen blog), states who it is for (screen reader users), and includes a directly verifiable acceptance criterion.

The goal specifies what to change and where (renaming the Hollowbrook RSVP form's Submit button to "Send my reply"), states who it is for (guests), and provides a checkable criterion that the button reads "Send my reply".
The goal only asks to make the Driftwood help centre "better" without specifying what is to be made or changed, and neither acceptance criterion names something concrete that can be seen or checked.
The task only says to update the Thimblevane shop without specifying which items are out of date, what changes to make, or any concrete acceptance criterion that a reviewer can check.

The goal only says to work on the reports without specifying what should be made or changed, so it could mean many different pieces of work and neither a builder nor a reviewer can tell what done looks like.

The goal and details only say to clean up a clunky sign-up flow without specifying what concrete changes to make, what to include or avoid, or any checkable criterion for what "clean up" means so a reviewer can tell done from not done.

None of the acceptance criteria name something concrete that can be seen or checked, since "looks great," "readers love it," and "an independent reviewer agrees" are subjective and do not let a reviewer tell done from not done.

The goal only asks to make the Orders page faster without specifying what to change or a measurable target, and none of the acceptance criteria describe something concrete that a reviewer can objectively check.

None of the acceptance criteria name a concrete, checkable outcome—they only state that the messages are clearer, everything about the form is good, and a reviewer agrees—so a reviewer cannot tell done from not done.
None of the acceptance criteria name anything concrete that can be seen or checked in the deliverable, relying only on subjective statements about quality, team happiness, and reviewer agreement.

The goal only asks to improve the app without specifying what to change, the details provide no concrete requirements or scope, and neither acceptance criterion names something observable that can be checked.

The goal and details only ask to tidy up anything that needs it without specifying what changes to make, where, or what to include or avoid, and neither criterion states an observable, verifiable check.

The task fails because the goal does not specify what is to be made or changed, the details provide no concrete scope or requirements, and the acceptance criteria ("Things work." and "An independent reviewer agrees.") name nothing verifiable.
The task only asks for "the usual updates" as every month without stating what changes to make, what to include or avoid, or any concrete observable criterion a reviewer could check.
